messages:
jamie: Heads-up — planning a small schema deploy Wednesday 02:00 UTC to add tx_index (int8) to ledger.partitioned_entries. Expected lock per shard ~3-6m, backfill ~10-15m for last 7d. Posting runbook + rollback. Please ack if you have objections or special constraints.

deploy-bot: @channel scheduled window opening: 2026-04-07T02:00:00Z. Reply with `deploy ack` to opt into automated rollout. I will pin service version `api@v2.14.3` for the change.

ricardo: ack. Curious about the lock handshake across 4 shards — can we stagger shard locks to avoid global latency spikes?

jamie: yes plan is staggered locks: shard order 2,0,1,3 with 30s gap. We only take exclusive lock on one shard at a time. Backfill uses async worker pool limited to 6 threads to avoid DB IO surge.

priya: please gate the feature behind ff:ledger.tx_index_enabled and rollout at 0% until backfill + canary pass. Also add a canary check for tail latency on reads.

alex: on read replicas — we should run the backfill on primary to avoid replication lag causing inconsistency for the short window. We'll monitor replica lag carefully.

jamie: agreed. Runbook (short):
```
- freeze writes to `ledger.tx_index` column via app feature flag before lock
- deploy migration v2 -> adds nullable column: `ALTER TABLE ledger.partitioned_entries ADD COLUMN tx_index bigint;`
- for each shard: acquire lock with holdpoint, run small validate check, then run backfill: `UPDATE ... WHERE tx_index IS NULL AND created_at >= now() - interval '7 days'` in batches of 5k
- verify sample queries return expected results (see smoke queries below)
- lift holdpoint + flip feature flag to 100% once all shards done
```

jamie: smoke queries (examples):
```
SELECT count(*) FROM ledger.partitioned_entries WHERE tx_index IS NULL AND created_at >= now() - interval '7 days';
SELECT tx_index FROM ledger.partitioned_entries WHERE id = '<sample-id>' LIMIT 1;
```

sasha: rollback / escape hatch notes? If backfill stalls or locks exceed 6m we abort and drop column? Dropping a partially-populated column is safe but we need to ensure app doesn't read it.

jamie: rollback plan:
```
- Run `ROLLBACK` if in-transaction failure during DDL (shouldn't happen; DDL is autocommit)
- If backfill fails mid-way: pause workers, mark feature flag to 0%, revert any in-flight read changes, and run compensating job to set tx_index = NULL for records touched in the failed window (we record job ids)
- As last resort: `ALTER TABLE ledger.partitioned_entries DROP COLUMN tx_index;` and revert service to previous code (api@v2.14.2 pinned by deploy-bot)
```

ricardo: who calls the abort? DB oncall or release lead? Recommend DB oncall approves lock acquisition and will be primary abort decision.

oncall-db: I will be oncall that window. I'll watch lock times and replica lag. If lock > 8m or replication lag > 30s for >2 consecutive checks, I will call abort. Add my pager number to runbook.

priya: add these monitoring checks to deploybot pre-checks:
- sample write latency < 150ms
- replica lag < 20s before starting each shard
- current row-change rate within expected baseline (±30%)

jamie: done. deploy-bot, can you run those prechecks and create holdpoint before the first shard lock?

deploy-bot: Prechecks: will run `latency_check`, `replica_lag_check`, `write_qps_baseline` 5m before window. I will create a holdpoint labeled `lock-acq-approval` and notify thread. To proceed, reply `proceed shard N` from release lead or `abort` from @oncall-db.

alex: tagging release lead @jamie (already here). I'll be around the window to help with queries and the small backfill job.

jamie: final notes: service pin `api@v2.14.3` during migration, FF off initially. Post-mortem/notes to /docs/releases/ledger-tx-index with timings and any fallbacks. If no objections by EOD today I'll push to deploy-bot schedule. :thumbsup:

ricardo: +1

priya: +1

sasha: +1

oncall-db: acknowledged. I'll standby.
